sentences.text: Changchengopterus is a non-pterodactyloid pterosaur discovered in Qinglong County, Hebei Province, China.
Scientists later described a second adult specimen containing lower jaws from the Paleontological Museum of Liaoning in 2011.
The type species Changchengopterus pani was named by Lü Junchang in 2009 based on fossils from the Callovian-aged Tiaojishan Formation.
The species name pani honors Pan Lijun, the collector who donated the fossil to science.
In its original description, the animal was placed in the family Rhamphorhynchidae as a primitive pterosaur related to Dorygnathus.
A 2010 study tentatively placed Changchengopterus in the family Wukongopteridae due to noted similarities.
However, a 2013 study found Changchengopterus outside Wukongopteridae but slightly closer to pterodactyloids within the group Monofenestrata.
Later, a 2017 analysis recovered Changchengopterus outside the group Monofenestrata.
A 2024 study included Changchengopterus within Pterodactyliformes, suggesting primitive monofenestratans are an evolutionary grade leading to Pterodactyloidea.
